chapters.title: Tell It Not in Gath
chapters.html:
Micah 1

The LORD Comes Out of His Place

1The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

2Hear, you peoples, all of you;
listen, earth, and all that fills it;
let the Lord GOD be a witness against you,
the Lord from His holy temple.

3For the LORD is about to come out from His place;
He will come down and tread on the heights of the earth.

4The mountains will melt under Him,
and the valleys split open,
like wax before the fire,
like water poured down a slope.

5All this is for the transgression of Jacob
and for the sins of the house of Israel.
What is the transgression of Jacob?
Is it not Samaria?
What are the high places of Judah?
Are they not Jerusalem?

6So I will make Samaria a heap in the open field,
a place for planting vineyards;
I will pour her stones down into the valley
and lay bare her foundations.

7All her carved images will be smashed to pieces,
all her wages will be burned with fire,
and I will make all her idols a desolation;
for she gathered them from a prostitute's wages,
and to a prostitute's wages they will return.

I Will Lament and Howl

8For this I will lament and howl;
I will go stripped and naked;
I will make a lament like the jackals
and a mourning like the ostriches.

9For her wounds are incurable;
it has come to Judah;
it has reached the gate of my people,
to Jerusalem.

10Tell it not in Gath;
do not weep at all;
in Beth-leaphrah
roll yourself in the dust.

11Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir,
in shameful nakedness;
the inhabitant of Zaanan has not come out;
the wailing of Beth-ezel
will take from you its standing place.

12For the inhabitant of Maroth
writhes, waiting for good,
because disaster has come down from the LORD
to the gate of Jerusalem.

13Harness the chariot to the steeds,
inhabitant of Lachish;
she was the beginning of sin
for the daughter of Zion,
for in you were found
the transgressions of Israel.

14Therefore you will give parting gifts
to Moresheth-gath;
the houses of Achzib will be a deceitful brook
to the kings of Israel.

15I will yet bring the conqueror upon you,
inhabitant of Mareshah;
the glory of Israel
will come as far as Adullam.

16Make yourself bald and shave your hair
for the children you delight in;
make your baldness as wide as the eagle's,
for they have gone from you into exile.

Notes

  • v1 "Micah of Moresheth… Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah" — Mikhah is short for Mikhayahu, who is like the LORD?, and Jeremiah's text writes it long, Mikhayah, where it is read Mikhah (Jeremiah 26:18). The Greek calls him Meichaias, the name it gives Micaiah son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He is remembered by name in Jeremiah's trial, when some of the elders of the land said, Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah (Jeremiah 26:17–18). The kings are those of Hosea 1:1 after Uzziah. Moresheth is the Moresheth-gath of v14.

  • v2 "Hear, you peoples, all of you" — shim'u ammim kullam, word for word the last words of Micaiah son of Imlah, Hear, all you peoples! (1 Kings 22:28). The earth and all that fills it is the psalm's The earth is the LORD's, and all that fills it (Psalm 24:1); here it is called to court.

  • vv3–4 "the LORD is about to come out from His place… tread on the heights of the earth… like wax before the fire" — ki hinneh YHWH yotse mi-meqomo, the words of Isaiah 26:21, For the LORD is about to come out from His place to punish the inhabitants of the earth. Treads on the heights of the earth is the line of Amos's hymn (Amos 4:13). The melting is the psalm's, The mountains melt like wax before the LORD (Psalm 97:5).

  • v5 "What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? What are the high places of Judah?" — the sin is named as the two capitals themselves. Bamot, high places, is the word of v3, bamotei arets, the heights the LORD treads: He comes down on the heights, and Judah's heights are Jerusalem. The Greek has what is the sin of the house of Judah?

  • vv6–7 "a heap in the open field… a prostitute's wages" — Micah says it of Jerusalem too, in the words Jeremiah's elders quote: Zion shall be plowed as a field; Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins (Jeremiah 26:18). Etnan, wages, three times, is the prostitute's pay the law would not let into the LORD's house (Deuteronomy 23:18), and Hosea's word, you have loved a prostitute's wages (Hosea 9:1).

  • vv8–9 "I will go stripped and naked… like the jackals… like the ostriches… her wounds are incurable" — sholal, stripped, the read form (written shilal), as in He leads counselors away stripped (Job 12:17); Isaiah walked naked and barefoot as a sign (Isaiah 20:2). Job mourned in the same pair, I am a brother of jackals and a companion of ostriches (Job 30:29). The Greek has she will lament: Samaria, not the prophet. Incurable is Jeremiah's word, my wound incurable (Jeremiah 15:18).

  • vv10–12 "Tell it not in Gath… Beth-leaphrah… Shaphir… Zaanan… Beth-ezel… Maroth" — Tell it not in Gath is David's lament for Saul (2 Samuel 1:20). Then each town hears its name turned against it: Beit le-Afrah, house of dust, rolls in afar, dust (the read form, roll yourself; written, I have rolled); Shafir, beautiful, goes in shameful nakedness; Tsa'anan sounds like yatsa, come out, and does not come out; Marot, bitterness, waits for good. V11's last line is obscure: Beit ha-Etsel, house beside, takes its emdah, standing place, away. The Greek reads several names as words.

  • vv13–14 "Lachish… the chariot to the steeds… parting gifts to Moresheth-gath… Achzib" — Lakhish chimes with rekhesh, steeds. Shilluchim, parting gifts, are a bride's dowry, as Pharaoh gave Gezer as a dowry to his daughter (1 Kings 9:16), and Moreshet sounds like me'orasah, engaged, the word of a virgin… engaged to a man (Deuteronomy 22:23): Micah's own town is given away like a bride. Akhziv… le-akhzav, a deceitful brook, a wadi that runs dry, Jeremiah's Will You be to me like a deceitful brook, like waters that fail? (Jeremiah 15:18).

  • v15 "the conqueror… Mareshah… Adullam" — ha-yoresh, the one who takes possession, and Mareshah sound alike. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam as David came when he fled, David left there and escaped to the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1).

  • v16 "Make yourself bald… as wide as the eagle's" — the mourner's shaved head (Amos 8:10), the bald patch… for the dead the law forbade (Deuteronomy 14:1). Nesher, the eagle of Hosea 8:1, is also the vulture, and the line compares the shaved head to its bare one.

chapters.title: The One Who Breaks Through
chapters.html:
Micah 2

Woe to Those Who Devise Wickedness

1Woe to those who devise wickedness
and work evil on their beds!
In the morning light they do it,
for their hand has the power.

2They covet fields and seize them,
and houses, and take them away;
they oppress a man and his house,
a man and his inheritance.

3Therefore this is what the LORD says:
I am about to devise disaster against this family,
from which you cannot remove your necks;
you will not walk with your heads high,
for it is an evil time.

4On that day they will take up a taunt against you
and raise a lament:
"It is over; we are utterly ruined;
He changes the portion of my people.
How He takes it away from me!
To the faithless He divides our fields."

5Therefore you will have no one
to cast the measuring line by lot
in the assembly of the LORD.

Do Not Preach

6"Do not preach," they preach.
"One should not preach of such things;
disgrace will not overtake us."

7Should this be said, house of Jacob?
Is the Spirit of the LORD cut short?
Are these His deeds?
Do not My words do good
to the one who walks uprightly?

8But lately My people have risen up as an enemy:
you strip the cloak off the garment
from those who pass by trusting,
like men returning from war.

9The women of My people you drive out
from their pleasant houses;
from their young children you take away
My splendor forever.

10Get up and go,
for this is not the place of rest;
because of uncleanness it will destroy
with a grievous destruction.

11If a man walking after wind and lies should deceive:
"I will preach to you of wine and strong drink,"
he would be the preacher for this people!

I Will Gather Jacob

12I will surely gather all of you, Jacob;
I will surely assemble the remnant of Israel;
I will put them together like sheep in a fold,
like a flock in the middle of its pasture;
they will hum with people.

13The one who breaks through will go up before them;
they will break through and pass the gate
and go out by it;
their king will pass on before them,
the LORD at their head.

Notes

  • vv1, 3 "those who devise wickedness… for their hand has the power… I am about to devise disaster" — choshvei aven, those who devise, and the LORD's answer with the same verb, hineni choshev, I am about to devise: their evil and His disaster are both ra. Yesh le-el yadam, their hand has the power, are Laban's words to Jacob, My hand has the power to do you harm (Genesis 31:29). The Greek reads el as God: because they did not lift their hands to God.

  • v2 "They covet fields and seize them… a man and his inheritance" — chamad, the verb of the commandment, You shall not covet your neighbor's house (Exodus 20:17). Nachalah, inheritance, is the family's share of the land, which the law says shall not be sold for good, because the land is Mine (Leviticus 25:23), and what Naboth refused the king, The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers (1 Kings 21:3).

  • vv3–5 "an evil time… He changes the portion of my people… the measuring line by lot" — ki et ra'ah hi, for it is an evil time, are Amos's words (Amos 5:13). Cheleq, the portion, is the family's lot of land; le-shovev, to the faithless, is the word of Jeremiah's Return, faithless sons (Jeremiah 3:14). The land was first shared by lot, Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the LORD, and there Joshua divided the land (Joshua 18:10); those who seized the fields will have no one left to cast the line for them.

  • v6 "'Do not preach,' they preach" — al tattifu yattifun. Nataf is drip, and of speech preach, the verb Amaziah used to Amos, do not preach against the house of Isaac (Amos 7:16). Who says it, the people to the prophets or one prophet to another, the line does not mark. Lo yissag kelimmot is disgrace will not overtake us, or disgrace will not turn back; the Greek has do not weep with tears.

  • v7 "Is the Spirit of the LORD cut short?" — ha-qatsar ruach YHWH. Qotser ruach, shortness of spirit, is the impatience of the people in Egypt who did not listen to Moses, out of shortness of breath (Exodus 6:9). The question is turned on the LORD: is He short of patience? The answer is His own: Do not My words do good to the one who walks uprightly? The Greek has his words.

  • vv8–9 "My people have risen up as an enemy… from their young children you take away My splendor forever" — obscure. As the lines stand, the powerful treat their own people as an enemy, stripping cloaks from travelers who expect no harm, as if they were spoil of war, and driving women and children from their houses. Hadari, My splendor, is the LORD's: what He gave the children is taken from them for good.

  • v10 "this is not the place of rest… with a grievous destruction" — menuchah, the rest promised with the land, you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance (Deuteronomy 12:9): those who seize the inheritance (v2) lose the rest. Chevel, destruction, sounds like chevel, the measuring line of v5.

  • v11 "If a man walking after wind and lies… I will preach to you of wine and strong drink" — attif, I will preach, is I will drip: he drips words of wine. Ruach is wind here, the emptiness Hosea gives Ephraim, Ephraim feeds on the wind (Hosea 12:1).

  • v12 "like sheep in a fold, like a flock in the middle of its pasture" — ke-tson botsrah: botsrah is a sheepfold, and also the name of Bozrah, the city of Edom (Amos 1:12); the Greek has like sheep in affliction. Dovro, its pasture, is Isaiah's word, Lambs shall graze as in their pasture (Isaiah 5:17). The promise follows the false preacher of v11 with no word of change between them.

  • v13 "The one who breaks through will go up before them… their king… the LORD at their head" — ha-porets, the one who breaks through, has the name of Perez, How you have breached — a breach upon you!… He called his name Perez (Genesis 38:29), from whom David came (Ruth 4:18), and the words of David's victory, The LORD has broken through my enemies before me (2 Samuel 5:20). Whether their king and the LORD are one leader or two, the verse does not say.

chapters.title: Zion Shall Be Plowed as a Field
chapters.html:
Micah 3

The Heads of Jacob

1I said:
Hear, please, you heads of Jacob
and rulers of the house of Israel!
Is it not for you to know justice?

2You who hate good and love evil,
who tear the skin off them
and the flesh off their bones,

3who eat the flesh of my people,
strip their skin off them,
break their bones,
and chop them up like meat for the pot,
like flesh in a cauldron —

4then they will cry out to the LORD,
but He will not answer them;
He will hide His face from them at that time,
because they have made their deeds evil.

The Prophets Who Lead My People Astray

5This is what the LORD says concerning the prophets
who lead My people astray,
who, when they have something to bite with their teeth,
cry "Peace!",
but consecrate war against whoever puts nothing into their mouths:

6Therefore it will be night for you, without vision,
and darkness for you, without divination;
the sun will go down on the prophets,
and the day will grow dark over them.

7The seers will be ashamed,
and the diviners disgraced;
they will all cover their upper lips,
for there is no answer from God.

8But as for me, I am filled with power,
with the Spirit of the LORD,
and with justice and might,
to declare to Jacob his transgression
and to Israel his sin.

Because of You

9Hear this, please, you heads of the house of Jacob
and rulers of the house of Israel,
who detest justice
and make crooked all that is straight,

10who build Zion with blood
and Jerusalem with injustice.

11Her heads judge for a bribe,
her priests teach for a price,
and her prophets divine for money;
yet they lean on the LORD and say,
"Is not the LORD among us?
No disaster will come upon us."

12Therefore, because of you,
Zion shall be plowed as a field;
Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins,
and the mountain of the house a wooded height.

Notes

  • v1 "I said: Hear, please, you heads of Jacob… Is it not for you to know justice?" — va-omar, I said: Micah speaks of himself for the first time. The heads and rulers are the ones whose work was to know mishpat, justice, the right judgment of a case, and v9 says they detest it.

  • vv2–3 "You who hate good and love evil… like meat for the pot" — the reverse of Amos's Hate evil and love good (Amos 5:15). The people are butchered and cooked: skin, flesh, bones, pot. In Ezekiel the rulers of Jerusalem boast, This city is the pot, and we are the meat (Ezekiel 11:3); here they are the cooks, and the people are the meat. My people is Micah's own word, as in the gate of my people (1:9).

  • v4 "He will hide His face from them" — the words of the law's warning, I will forsake them and hide My face from them (Deuteronomy 31:17). They cried no prayer while they ate; they will cry and not be answered.

  • v5 "who, when they have something to bite with their teeth, cry 'Peace!'" — ha-noshkhim be-shinneihem, word for word who bite with their teeth; nashakh is the verb of the snake's bite (Amos 5:19; 9:3). A meal buys shalom, the word Jeremiah's prophets sold, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace (Jeremiah 6:14). No meal, and they consecrate war, the holy war of Consecrate war against her! (Jeremiah 6:4).

  • vv6–7 "night for you, without vision… they will all cover their upper lips" — night comes on the prophets with no vision in it, and the sun goes down on them as in Amos 8:9. To cover the upper lip is the sign of one cut off: he shall cover his upper lip and call out, "Unclean! Unclean!" (Leviticus 13:45), and of mourning, which Ezekiel was told to refuse, do not cover your upper lip (Ezekiel 24:17). Ma'aneh, answer, is from the verb of v4: the LORD will not answer the rulers, and He will not answer the prophets.

  • v8 "But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD" — et ruach YHWH, the Spirit set between power and justice; the Greek has in the Spirit of the Lord. Against prophets who speak for food (v5) and for money (v11), Micah's fullness is the Spirit, and what it fills him for is to name sin. Another prophet was asked the same question with a slap, Which way did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you? (1 Kings 22:24), the Micaiah whose words open this book (1:2).

  • vv9–10 "who detest justice and make crooked all that is straight… who build Zion with blood" — meta'avim, who detest, is the verb of they detest the one who speaks with integrity (Amos 5:10), the root of detestable. Ye'aqqeshu, make crooked, is the law's word for a crooked and twisted generation (Deuteronomy 32:5). Boneh, who builds, is singular, as in Jeremiah's woe, Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness (Jeremiah 22:13).

  • v11 "Her heads judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price… Is not the LORD among us?" — the law said you shall not take a bribe (Deuteronomy 16:19), and yoru, teach, is the verb of torah: instruction sold. Their boast reverses the cry the law foretold, Is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us? (Deuteronomy 31:17); they say the LORD is among them, so no disaster will find them.

  • v12 "Zion shall be plowed as a field… a wooded height" — this verse is quoted word for word in Jeremiah's trial: Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah… Zion shall be plowed as a field (Jeremiah 26:18). The elders go on: Did he not fear the LORD and plead with the LORD, so that the LORD relented of the disaster that He had pronounced against them? (Jeremiah 26:19). Bamot ya'ar, a wooded height, says bamot again, the heights of 1:3 and 1:5.

chapters.title: Swords into Plowshares
chapters.html:
Micah 4

The Mountain of the LORD's House

1And it shall come to pass in the last days
that the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established
as the highest of the mountains;
it shall be lifted up above the hills,
and peoples shall stream to it.

2Many nations shall go and say,
"Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD,
and to the house of the God of Jacob,
that He may teach us His ways,
and that we may walk in His paths."
For out of Zion shall go forth instruction,
and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

3He shall judge between many peoples,
and decide for strong nations far away;
they shall beat their swords into plowshares,
and their spears into pruning hooks;
nation shall not lift up sword against nation,
nor shall they learn war anymore.

4But they shall sit, each man under his vine
and under his fig tree,
and no one shall make them afraid;
for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.

5For all the peoples walk,
each in the name of its god,
but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God
forever and ever.

The Lame and the Outcast

6On that day, declares the LORD,
I will gather the lame
and assemble the outcast,
and those I have harmed;

7I will make the lame a remnant,
and the cast-off a strong nation;
and the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion
from now on and forever.

8As for you, tower of the flock,
hill of the daughter of Zion,
to you it will come;
the former dominion will come,
the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.

Writhe, Daughter of Zion

9Now why do you cry aloud?
Is there no king in you?
Has your counselor perished,
that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?

10Writhe and burst forth, daughter of Zion,
like a woman in labor;
for now you will go out of the city
and live in the open field;
you will go to Babylon;
there you will be rescued;
there the LORD will redeem you
from the power of your enemies.

11Now many nations are gathered against you,
who say, "Let her be polluted,
and let our eyes gaze on Zion."

12But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD,
and they do not understand His counsel,
for He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.

13Rise and thresh, daughter of Zion,
for I will make your horn iron
and your hoofs bronze;
you will crush many peoples,
and I will devote their gain to the LORD,
their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "the mountain of the LORD's house… swords into plowshares" — the same oracle stands in Isaiah 2:2–4, nearly word for word, and the English here follows Isaiah's where the Hebrew is the same. The two differ in small things that show: here peoples shall stream to it, where Isaiah has all the nations; many nations shall go, where Isaiah has many peoples; and Micah alone has strong nations far away. Isaiah goes on, House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the LORD (Isaiah 2:5); Micah goes on with v4. Be-acharit ha-yamim, in the last days, is the phrase Hosea gives as in the end of days (Hosea 3:5).

  • v4 "each man under his vine and under his fig tree… no one shall make them afraid" — the words of Solomon's peace, each man under his vine and under his fig tree (1 Kings 4:25), and of the law's blessing, you will lie down with no one to make you afraid (Leviticus 26:6). For the mouth of the LORD has spoken is Isaiah's seal on a word (Isaiah 1:20).

  • v5 "each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the LORD" — v1 saw the peoples streaming to Zion in the last days; v5 speaks of the present, when each still walks after its own god, and says what Israel will do now.

  • vv6–7 "I will gather the lame… the cast-off a strong nation" — ha-tsole'ah, the lame, is the word for Jacob after the night at Penuel, he was limping on his hip (Genesis 32:31): the people are gathered limping, as their father walked away. Va-asher hare'oti, those I have harmed: the LORD names the harm as His own (2:3). Will reign is the song's The LORD will reign forever and ever (Exodus 15:18).

  • v8 "tower of the flock, hill of the daughter of Zion" — Migdal Eder, Tower of the Flock, is the place where Jacob camped after Rachel was buried on the road to Ephrath — that is Bethlehem: Israel pulled up and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder (Genesis 35:19, 21). Ophel, hill, is the name of a height of Jerusalem, the wall of Ophel (2 Chronicles 27:3). The former dominion is the kingdom as it once was; the Greek adds from Babylon.

  • vv9–10 "Is there no king in you?… you will go to Babylon; there the LORD will redeem you" — the king may be Jerusalem's own, beside your counselor, or the LORD, who has just been named as reigning on Mount Zion (v7), as Jeremiah hears the exiles ask, Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her King not in her? (Jeremiah 8:19). Gochi, burst forth, is the verb of the sea born from the womb, when it burst out from the womb (Job 38:8). Micah names Babylon here, though the enemy at the door in his own oracles is Assyria (5:5–6); and the way out runs through the exile itself: there she is rescued. Yig'alekh, will redeem you, is the verb of the kinsman who buys back.

  • vv11–12 "Let her be polluted… like sheaves to the threshing floor" — techenaf, polluted, is the law's word, You shall not pollute the land where you are (Numbers 35:33). Machshevot, thoughts, is from the verb of 2:1 and 2:3, devise: the nations devise against Zion, and the LORD's thoughts are not theirs, as in My thoughts are not your thoughts (Isaiah 55:8). They gather themselves for war, and He has gathered them as a farmer gathers sheaves for threshing.

  • v13 "I will make your horn iron… I will devote their gain to the LORD" — horns of iron were the sign of the false prophet Zedekiah (1 Kings 22:11); here the LORD gives them. Ve-hacharamti, I will devote, is the word for what is given wholly to the LORD: Zion threshes, and the LORD takes the spoil for Himself. The Greek has you will devote, keeping the subject of you will crush. Betsa, gain, is the word of men… who hate dishonest gain (Exodus 18:21), and the Lord of all the earth is the title of the ark at the Jordan, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth (Joshua 3:11).

speech.text: Micah 4
The Mountain of the LORD's House

And it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established as the highest of the mountains; it shall be lifted up above the hills, and peoples shall stream to it.

Many nations shall go and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob, that He may teach us His ways, and that we may walk in His paths." For out of Zion shall go forth instruction, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He shall judge between many peoples, and decide for strong nations far away; they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn war anymore.
But they shall sit, each man under his vine and under his fig tree, and no one shall make them afraid; for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.
For all the peoples walk, each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
The Lame and the Outcast
On that day, declares the LORD, I will gather the lame and assemble the outcast, and those I have harmed;
I will make the lame a remnant, and the cast-off a strong nation; and the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on and forever.
As for you, tower of the flock, hill of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come; the former dominion will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
Writhe, Daughter of Zion
Now why do you cry aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?

Writhe and burst forth, daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor; for now you will go out of the city and live in the open field; you will go to Babylon; there you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the power of your enemies.
Now many nations are gathered against you, who say, "Let her be polluted, and let our eyes gaze on Zion."
But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD, and they do not understand His counsel, for He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.

Rise and thresh, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hoofs bronze; you will crush many peoples, and I will devote their gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.

chapters.title: But You, Bethlehem Ephrathah
chapters.html:
Micah 5

The Ruler from Bethlehem

1Now gather in your troops, daughter of troops;
a siege is laid against us;
with a rod they strike the judge of Israel
on the cheek.

2But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah,
too small to be among the clans of Judah,
from you shall come out for Me
one who is to be ruler in Israel,
whose goings out are from ancient times,
from the days of old.

3Therefore He will give them up
until the time when she who is in labor has given birth;
then the rest of his brothers will return
to the sons of Israel.

4He will stand and shepherd in the strength of the LORD,
in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God;
and they will live secure,
for now he will be great
to the ends of the earth.

5This one will be peace.
When Assyria comes into our land
and treads on our strongholds,
we will raise against him seven shepherds
and eight princes of men.

6They will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword,
and the land of Nimrod at its gates;
and he will rescue us from Assyria
when it comes into our land
and treads within our border.

The Remnant of Jacob

7The remnant of Jacob will be
among many peoples
like dew from the LORD,
like downpours on the plants,
which do not wait for man
or delay for the sons of men.

8The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations,
among many peoples,
like a lion among the beasts of the forest,
like a young lion among the flocks of sheep,
which, when it goes through, tramples and tears,
and there is no one to rescue.

9Your hand will be lifted up over your adversaries,
and all your enemies will be cut off.

I Will Cut Off

10And it shall come to pass on that day,
declares the LORD,
that I will cut off your horses from among you
and destroy your chariots;

11I will cut off the cities of your land
and tear down all your fortresses;

12I will cut off sorceries from your hand,
and you will have no more soothsayers;

13I will cut off your carved images
and your standing stones from among you,
and you will no longer bow down
to the work of your hands;

14I will uproot your sacred poles from among you
and destroy your cities.

15In anger and wrath I will execute vengeance
on the nations that have not listened.

Notes

  • v1 "Now gather in your troops, daughter of troops… strike the judge of Israel on the cheek" — in the Hebrew text this verse is 4:14, and vv2–15 are 5:1–14; the English numbering is followed. Titgodedi bat gedud plays on one sound: gadad is to gather in troops, as Jeremiah's people trooped to the house of a prostitute (Jeremiah 5:7), and to gash oneself in grief, You shall not gash yourselves (Deuteronomy 14:1). The Greek has the daughter will be walled in with a wall. The judge struck on the cheek is how the prophet before Micah was treated: Zedekiah… struck Micaiah on the cheek (1 Kings 22:24). From the shofet, judge, struck down, the next verse turns to the moshel, ruler, to come.

  • v2 "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too small to be among the clans of Judah" — Ephrathah is David's town, that Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah whose name was Jesse (1 Samuel 17:12), and the road where Rachel was buried, the road to Ephrath — that is Bethlehem (Genesis 35:19). Tsa'ir, small, is the word for the younger son in the oracle over Rebekah's twins, the elder shall serve the younger (Genesis 25:23). Matthew gives the verse in other words: You, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you will come a ruler who will shepherd My people Israel (Matthew 2:6). Alfei, the clans, has the letters of allufei, chiefs; by no means least turns too small around; and who will shepherd My people Israel are the words said to David, You shall shepherd My people Israel (2 Samuel 5:2).

  • v2 "whose goings out are from ancient times, from the days of old" — motsa'otav, his goings out, the word of Israel's starting points in the wilderness (Numbers 33:2): where he comes from. Mi-yemei olam, from the days of old, are the words of Amos's promise to rebuild David's fallen booth as in the days of old (Amos 9:11). Olam runs from long ago to forever: Micah has it as forever and ever (4:5) and from now on and forever (4:7).

  • v3 "until the time when she who is in labor has given birth" — yoledah yaladah, she who bears has borne. The daughter of Zion was just told to writhe… like a woman in labor (4:10); she may be the one, or the ruler's own mother; the verse does not name her. The rest of his brothers are the scattered ones gathered in 4:6–7.

  • v4 "He will stand and shepherd in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD" — the shepherd-king of the promise to David (2 Samuel 5:2), as in Ezekiel's one shepherd… My servant David (Ezekiel 34:23). Ge'on, majesty, is the word of the pride of Jacob (Amos 6:8; 8:7): there the pride was Jacob's, here it belongs to the LORD's name. To the ends of the earth, ad afsei arets, is the reach of Joseph's horns in Moses' blessing (Deuteronomy 33:17).

  • vv5–6 "This one will be peace… seven shepherds and eight princes of men… the land of Nimrod" — ve-hayah zeh shalom: zeh, this one, the ruler of vv2–4, or this of what follows; the Greek has this will be peace. Seven, then eight, is the counting of Amos's for three… and for four (Amos 1:3): enough, and one more. Nesikhei, princes, is the word of the princes of Sihon (Joshua 13:21). Assyria is called the land of Nimrod, from whose kingdom went out Asshur (Genesis 10:11). Shepherd… with the sword is the shepherd's word turned to war. Bi-ftacheha, at its gates; the Greek has in its trench.

  • vv7–8 "like dew from the LORD… like a lion among the beasts of the forest" — two pictures of one remnant. The first is Moses' song, my speech distill like the dew, like showers on the new grass, like downpours on the plants (Deuteronomy 32:2), and Hosea's I will be like the dew to Israel (Hosea 14:5): rain that waits for no one. The second is Jacob's blessing of Judah, like a lion, and like a lioness — who will rouse him? (Genesis 49:9), and Hosea's lion turned around: there the LORD said I Myself will tear… and no one will rescue against Israel (Hosea 5:14); here the remnant tears, and there is no one to rescue.

  • vv10–14 "I will cut off your horses… sorceries… your standing stones… your sacred poles" — ve-hikhratti, I will cut off, four times, and what is cut off is what Israel trusted: horses, which the king was not to multiply (Deuteronomy 17:16); walled cities; a soothsayer… or a sorcerer (Deuteronomy 18:10); standing stones and sacred poles, You shall not plant for yourself a sacred pole (Deuteronomy 16:21). It is the list Hosea's penitents give up in their own mouths, we will not ride on horses; and we will no longer say 'Our God' to the work of our hands (Hosea 14:3).

  • v15 "on the nations that have not listened" — asher lo shame'u, who have not heard: the book opened with Hear, you peoples, all of you (1:2), and the nations who go up to be taught (4:2) are set against those who would not hear.

chapters.title: What the LORD Requires
chapters.html:
Micah 6

The LORD's Case

1Hear, please, what the LORD says:
Rise, plead your case before the mountains,
and let the hills hear your voice.

2Hear, you mountains, the LORD's case,
you enduring foundations of the earth;
for the LORD has a case against His people,
and He will argue it out with Israel.

3My people, what have I done to you?
How have I wearied you?
Answer against Me!

4For I brought you up from the land of Egypt
and redeemed you from the house of slaves;
and I sent before you
Moses, Aaron and Miriam.

5My people, remember what Balak king of Moab devised,
and what Balaam son of Beor answered him,
from Shittim to Gilgal,
so that you may know the righteous acts of the LORD.

What Does the LORD Require?

6With what shall I come before the LORD
and bow myself before God on high?
Shall I come before Him with burnt offerings,
with calves a year old?

7Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams,
with ten thousands of rivers of oil?
Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression,
the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?

8He has told you, O man, what is good;
and what does the LORD require of you
but to do justice, and to love loyal love,
and to walk humbly with your God?

Wicked Scales

9The voice of the LORD calls to the city,
and sound wisdom sees Your name:
Hear the rod, and the One who appointed it!

10Are there still, in the house of the wicked,
treasures of wickedness,
and the scant ephah that is cursed?

11Shall I count pure the one with wicked scales,
with a bag of false weights?

12Her rich men are full of violence;
her inhabitants speak lies,
and their tongue is deceit in their mouth.

13So I in turn have struck you with a sickening blow,
making you desolate because of your sins.

14You will eat and not be satisfied,
and your hunger will be inside you;
you will put away but not save,
and what you save I will give to the sword.

15You will sow but not reap;
you will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil,
and tread grapes for new wine but not drink the wine.

16The statutes of Omri are kept,
and all the works of the house of Ahab,
and you have walked in their counsels;
so I will make you a desolation,
and her inhabitants a thing to be hissed at,
and you will bear the scorn of My people.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "plead your case before the mountains… the LORD has a case against His people" — riv, a case at law, as in Hosea's the LORD has a case against the inhabitants of the land (Hosea 4:1). The mountains are the witnesses, the oldest things there are, as Moses called the heavens and the earth, Give ear, heavens… let the earth hear the words of my mouth (Deuteronomy 32:1). Ha-etanim, enduring, is the word of righteousness like an ever-flowing stream (Amos 5:24). Yitvakkach, He will argue it out, is the verb of Come now, let us settle this (Isaiah 1:18).

  • vv3–4 "How have I wearied you? Answer against Me!… I brought you up" — aneh vi, answer against Me, is the courtroom verb of the commandment, You shall not answer against your neighbor as a false witness (Exodus 20:16): the LORD invites Israel to testify against Him. Hel'etikha, I wearied you, and he'elitikha, I brought you up, sound nearly alike: the charge Israel could bring, and the answer. From the house of slaves is the opening of the commandments (Exodus 20:2), and redeemed you from the house of slaves is Moses' word (Deuteronomy 7:8). Miriam is sent with her brothers, Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister (Exodus 15:20).

  • v5 "Balak king of Moab… Balaam son of Beor… from Shittim to Gilgal" — Balak sent for Balaam to call him… come and curse this people for me (Numbers 22:5–6), and Balaam could only bless. From Shittim to Gilgal is the crossing of the Jordan: they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan (Joshua 3:1), and camped at Gilgal on the far side (Joshua 4:19). Tsidqot YHWH, the righteous acts of the LORD, is Samuel's phrase as he too put the people on trial, I may plead with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD (1 Samuel 12:7).

  • vv6–7 "calves a year old… thousands of rams… Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression?" — the offerings climb: the calf of the law, a calf and a lamb, both a year old (Leviticus 9:3), then thousands, then the firstborn child. The last was done in Micah's own days: King Ahaz, one of the three kings of 1:1, made his son pass through the fire (2 Kings 16:3), as the king of Moab, Balak's land, took his firstborn son… and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall (2 Kings 3:27).

  • v8 "what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love loyal love, and to walk humbly with your God?" — Moses asked it first: And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways and to love Him (Deuteronomy 10:12). Ahavat chesed, to love loyal love, is the chesed the LORD desires over sacrifice, For I desire loyal love and not sacrifice (Hosea 6:6), and the chesed He delights in (7:18). Hatsnea lekhet, to walk humbly, from tsana, modest, careful, as in with the humble is wisdom (Proverbs 11:2); the Greek has to be ready to walk with the Lord your God. Adam, O man: a human being, any one.

  • v9 "sound wisdom sees Your name: Hear the rod, and the One who appointed it!" — obscure. Ve-tushiyyah yir'eh shemekha, and sound wisdom sees Your name; yir'eh, sees, has the letters of yir'ah, fear, and the Greek has He will save those who fear His name. Shim'u matteh u-mi ye'adah, hear the rod, and who appointed it: matteh is a rod and also a tribe, and the Greek has hear, O tribe. Ye'adah, appointed it, is feminine, which may point back to the city. As the lines stand, the rod is the punishment, and the city is told to heed it and the One who set it.

  • vv10–11 "Are there still… the scant ephah… a bag of false weights" — od ha-ish: ish is a spelling of yesh, there is, as in the wise woman's words to David (2 Samuel 14:19); the Greek has fire, esh, nearly the same letters. The weights are the law's, You shall not have in your bag two kinds of weights (Deuteronomy 25:13) and two kinds of ephah (25:14), and Hosea's false scales (Hosea 12:7), the same mirmah, false.

  • vv13–15 "a sickening blow… You will eat and not be satisfied… you will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil" — the curses of the law come due: you will eat and not be satisfied (Leviticus 26:26), and you will not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will drop off (Deuteronomy 28:40), as Amos also said of the vineyards (Amos 5:11). Ve-yeshchakha, your hunger, is found only here, and its sense is a guess from the line; the Greek has it will grow dark in you.

  • v16 "The statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab" — the kings of the north: Omri… did more evil than all who were before him (1 Kings 16:25), and there was none like Ahab, who sold himself to do what was evil (1 Kings 21:25). Ve-yishtammer chuqqot, the statutes… are kept, and va-telkhu, you have walked, are the words of the law, keep My statutes, and walk in them (Leviticus 18:4), turned to Omri's. A thing to be hissed at is Jeremiah's word of the ruined city (Jeremiah 19:8). Cherpat ammi, the scorn of My people; the Greek has the scorn of peoples.

chapters.title: Who Is a God Like You?
chapters.html:
Micah 7

Woe to Me

1Woe to me! For I have become
like the gatherings of summer fruit,
like the gleanings of the grape harvest:
there is no cluster to eat,
no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.

2The faithful one has perished from the land,
and there is no one upright among men;
they all lie in wait for blood;
each hunts his brother with a net.

3Their hands are on evil, to do it well:
the prince asks, and the judge, for a payment,
and the great man speaks the desire of his soul;
so they weave it together.

4The best of them is like a briar,
the most upright worse than a hedge of thorns.
The day of your watchmen, your punishment, has come;
now will be their confusion.

5Do not trust a neighbor;
do not rely on a close friend;
from her who lies in your arms
guard the doors of your mouth.

6For son treats father with contempt,
daughter rises against her mother,
daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;
a man's enemies are the men of his own house.

I Will Watch for the LORD

7But as for me, I will watch for the LORD;
I will wait for the God of my salvation;
my God will hear me.

8Do not rejoice over me, my enemy;
though I have fallen, I will rise;
though I sit in darkness,
the LORD is my light.

9I will bear the rage of the LORD,
because I have sinned against Him,
until He pleads my cause
and carries out justice for me.
He will bring me out to the light;
I will look on His righteousness.

10Then my enemy will see,
and shame will cover her,
she who said to me,
"Where is the LORD your God?"
My eyes will look on her;
now she will be trampled down
like the mud of the streets.

A Day for Building Your Walls

11A day for building your walls!
On that day the boundary will be far off.

12On that day they will come to you,
from Assyria and the cities of Egypt,
and from Egypt to the River,
from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.

13But the earth will become a desolation
because of its inhabitants,
for the fruit of their deeds.

Who Is a God Like You?

14Shepherd Your people with Your rod,
the flock of Your inheritance,
who dwell alone, a forest
in the middle of Carmel;
let them graze in Bashan and Gilead
as in the days of old.

15As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt,
I will show him wonders.

16The nations will see and be ashamed
of all their might;
they will lay their hand on their mouth;
their ears will be deaf.

17They will lick the dust like a snake,
like things that crawl on the earth;
they will come quaking out of their strongholds;
they will come trembling to the LORD our God,
and they will fear You.

18Who is a God like You,
carrying guilt and passing over transgression
for the remnant of His inheritance?
He does not hold on to His anger forever,
for He delights in loyal love.

19He will again have compassion on us;
He will tread our iniquities under foot.
You will cast all their sins
into the depths of the sea.

20You will give truth to Jacob,
loyal love to Abraham,
as You swore to our fathers
from ancient days.

Notes

  • v1 "Woe to me!… like the gleanings of the grape harvest… no first-ripe fig" — alelai li, woe to me, are Job's words, If I am guilty, woe to me! (Job 10:15). The prophet is a field after the harvest: qayits, summer fruit, is what Amos saw in the basket, a basket of summer fruit (Amos 8:1), and olelot batsir, the gleanings of the grape harvest, the little left on the vine, as at the gleaning when the grape harvest is done (Isaiah 24:13). Bikkurah is a first-ripe fig before the summer (Isaiah 28:4). He goes looking for one good person and finds none (v2).

  • v2 "The faithful one has perished… each hunts his brother with a net" — chasid, the faithful one, is from chesed, the loyal love the LORD requires (6:8), as in Save, LORD, for the faithful one is gone (Psalm 12:1). Cherem, a net, as in a place for spreading nets (Ezekiel 26:5), has the letters of cherem, a thing devoted to the LORD, the word of I will devote their gain to the LORD (4:13).

  • vv3–4 "the judge, for a payment… so they weave it together… worse than a hedge of thorns" — partly obscure. Ba-shillum, for a payment, is the word of Hosea's the days of repayment have come (Hosea 9:7). Va-ye'abbetuha, they weave it together, is found only here; it is the root of avot, a cord, as in bands of love (Hosea 11:4): the prince, the judge and the great man twist their wants into one rope. Mesukhah, a hedge of thorns, is the word of the way of a sluggard is like a hedge of thorns (Proverbs 15:19), spelled there with sin for samekh; and chedeq, briar, is the thorn of that verse; for like a briar the Greek has like a moth devouring. Your watchmen are the prophets, as the LORD said to Ezekiel, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel (Ezekiel 3:17): the day they warned of has come. Mevukhatam, their confusion, is Isaiah's a day of tumult and trampling and confusion (Isaiah 22:5).

  • vv5–6 "Do not trust a neighbor… a man's enemies are the men of his own house" — Jeremiah says the same of his city, Let everyone beware of his neighbor, and put no trust in any brother (Jeremiah 9:4). Alluf, close friend, is the word of a whisperer separates close friends (Proverbs 16:28). Matthew gives v6 in Jesus' words: For I came to set a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; and a man's enemies will be the members of his own household (Matthew 10:35–36).

  • vv7–10 "I will watch for the LORD… though I have fallen, I will rise… Where is the LORD your God?" — atsappeh, I will watch, is the verb of the watchmen of v4: they watched for the day of punishment, and the prophet watches for the LORD, as in in the morning I set it out before You, and watch (Psalm 5:3). Elohayikh, your God (v10), is said to a woman: the one who speaks now is the city, and oyavti, my enemy, is a woman too, another city. I have fallen, I will rise answers Amos's lament, Fallen, no more to rise, is virgin Israel (Amos 5:2). Yariv rivi, He pleads my cause, as in plead my cause against an unfaithful nation (Psalm 43:1): the LORD who had a case against His people (6:2) takes up their case. The enemy's taunt is the psalm's, Where is your God? (Psalm 42:3), and her end is the word of Isaiah, to trample them down like the mud of the streets (Isaiah 10:6).

  • vv11–13 "the boundary will be far off… from Assyria and the cities of Egypt… from sea to sea" — yirchak choq is obscure. Choq is a decree, and a boundary set, as in when He assigned to the sea its limit (Proverbs 8:29); so the boundary moves far out, or the decree is taken far away. The Greek has that day will rub away your statutes. Matsor, Egypt, is the name in the streams of Egypt (Isaiah 19:6), and it is also the word siege (5:1): those who once laid siege send the people home. The Greek has from Tyre. From sea to sea… the River is the reach of the king's rule in May he rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth (Psalm 72:8). Ha-arets is the land and the earth; here it follows the lands of v12, and is given as the earth. The fruit of their deeds is Jeremiah's phrase (Jeremiah 17:10).

  • v14 "Shepherd Your people with Your rod… who dwell alone… as in the days of old" — the prayer turns to the LORD. Shevet, rod, is the shepherd's rod of Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me (Psalm 23:4), and the rod that struck the judge on the cheek (5:1). Shokhni levadad, who dwell alone, are Balaam's words, Here is a people that lives alone (Numbers 23:9), and Moses', Israel dwells in safety, the fountain of Jacob alone (Deuteronomy 33:28). Bashan and Gilead are the grazing lands across the Jordan, the place was a place for livestock (Numbers 32:1). Kimei olam, as in the days of old, are the words of the ruler's beginnings (5:2).

  • vv15–17 "I will show him wonders… they will lick the dust like a snake… come trembling to the LORD our God" — the LORD answers: I will do wonders was His word to Moses (Exodus 34:10). The nations are struck silent, as Job was, I lay my hand on my mouth (Job 40:4), and brought low as the snake, dust you shall eat (Genesis 3:14), and as the king's enemies lick the dust (Psalm 72:9). Ke-zochalei arets, like things that crawl, is the word of things that crawl in the dust (Deuteronomy 32:24). Out of their strongholds is the psalm's come trembling out of their strongholds (Psalm 18:45), and yifchadu el YHWH, they will come trembling to the LORD, is Hosea's promise for Israel, they will come trembling to the LORD (Hosea 3:5), here given to the nations.

  • vv18–19 "Who is a God like You, carrying guilt and passing over transgression… into the depths of the sea" — mi el kamokha is the song at the sea, Who is like You among the gods, LORD? (Exodus 15:11), and the question in the prophet's own name: Mikhah is written Mikhayah in Jeremiah 26:18, who is like YH?, and Micaiah son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8) bears the same name. Nose avon, carrying guilt, is the name the LORD proclaimed, carrying guilt and rebellion and sin (Exodus 34:7). Over al pesha, passing over transgression, is the phrase of it is his glory to overlook an offense (Proverbs 19:11); Amos heard I will never again pass them by (Amos 7:8), and here the LORD passes over the sin instead. La-ad, forever, has the letters of le-ed, for a witness, and the Greek has He did not keep His anger as a witness. Yikhbosh, He will tread under foot, is the verb of fill the earth and take it under foot (Genesis 1:28). Metsulot, depths, is the sea where Pharaoh's army sank, They went down into the depths like a stone (Exodus 15:5). The Hebrew has their sins where the Greek has our sins.

  • v20 "You will give truth to Jacob, loyal love to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers" — emet and chesed, the pair of the LORD's name, abundant in loyal love and truth (Exodus 34:6), and of the blessing of Abraham's servant, who has not forsaken His kindness and His truth from my master (Genesis 24:27). The oath is the one sworn to Abraham, By Myself I have sworn (Genesis 22:16). Mi-mei qedem, from ancient days: qedem is the word of the ruler's goings out… from ancient times (5:2).

speech.text: Micah 7
Woe to Me
Woe to me! For I have become like the gatherings of summer fruit, like the gleanings of the grape harvest: there is no cluster to eat, no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.
The faithful one has perished from the land, and there is no one upright among men; they all lie in wait for blood; each hunts his brother with a net.
Their hands are on evil, to do it well: the prince asks, and the judge, for a payment, and the great man speaks the desire of his soul; so they weave it together.
The best of them is like a briar, the most upright worse than a hedge of thorns. The day of your watchmen, your punishment, has come; now will be their confusion.
Do not trust a neighbor; do not rely on a close friend; from her who lies in your arms guard the doors of your mouth.
For son treats father with contempt, daughter rises against her mother, daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house.
I Will Watch for the LORD
But as for me, I will watch for the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy; though I have fallen, I will rise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD is my light.
I will bear the rage of the LORD, because I have sinned against Him, until He pleads my cause and carries out justice for me. He will bring me out to the light; I will look on His righteousness.
Then my enemy will see, and shame will cover her, she who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" My eyes will look on her; now she will be trampled down like the mud of the streets.
A Day for Building Your Walls
A day for building your walls! On that day the boundary will be far off.
On that day they will come to you, from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
But the earth will become a desolation because of its inhabitants, for the fruit of their deeds.
Who Is a God Like You?
Shepherd Your people with Your rod, the flock of Your inheritance, who dwell alone, a forest in the middle of Carmel; let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might; they will lay their hand on their mouth; their ears will be deaf.
They will lick the dust like a snake, like things that crawl on the earth; they will come quaking out of their strongholds; they will come trembling to the LORD our God, and they will fear You.
Who is a God like You, carrying guilt and passing over transgression for the remnant of His inheritance? He does not hold on to His anger forever, for He delights in loyal love.
He will again have compassion on us; He will tread our iniquities under foot. You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
You will give truth to Jacob, loyal love to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from ancient days.
